findings.title: MetricAlertDetectorHandler is abstract and cannot be instantiated
findings.body: MetricAlertDetectorHandler now subclasses StatefulDetectorHandler (an abc.ABC) via `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass`, but does not implement the required abstract members `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, or `build_occurrence_and_event_data`. Previously this class was concrete because it implemented a stub `evaluate()`. Now, any code path that resolves `Detector.detector_handler` for a detector of type `metric_alert_fire` (e.g. via `group_type.detector_handler(self)` in `src/sentry/workflow_engine/models/detector.py`) will raise `TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class MetricAlertDetectorHandler with abstract methods ...` at runtime instead of returning a usable (even if no-op) handler. This is a regression from a working no-op handler to a handler that crashes on instantiation.

findings.title: Stale docstring says evaluate returns a list
findings.body: The docstring of `StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate` still states 'Evaluates a given data packet and returns a list of `DetectorEvaluationResult`', but the method signature and implementation were changed in this PR to return `dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]`. The abstract `DetectorHandler.evaluate` also still implies list semantics in neighboring comments. This is misleading for implementers of custom detector handlers.

findings.title: Removed duplicate-group-key test with no replacement coverage
findings.body: The previous test `test_state_results_multi_group_dupe`, which verified that `process_detectors` logged an error when a detector handler returned duplicate group keys, was deleted and not replaced with an equivalent test for the new dict-based `evaluate()` contract. Since `evaluate()` now returns a dict, a handler that computes the same group_key twice (e.g. due to a bug in `get_group_key_values` or a custom `DetectorHandler.evaluate` implementation) will silently have one result overwritten with no error/log, losing the previous diagnostic signal. There's no test asserting this new silent-overwrite behavior is acceptable, nor any safeguard reproduced for it.
